LESSON: WRITING 5.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING - PLAYS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing - Plays

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing - Plays. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does a play differ from a story?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the features of a play for information
2. write a short play based on the theme for communication
3. recognise the contribution of playwriting in the preservation of culture

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 5.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING - PLAYS
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing - Plays helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 5.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING - PLAYS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Explain the features of a play for information

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the features of a play for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the features of a play for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing - Plays”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the features of a play for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write a short play based on the theme for communication

What this means
In this part you learn to write a short play based on the theme for communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a short play based on the theme for communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing - Plays to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a short play based on the theme for communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Recognise the contribution of playwriting in the preservation of culture

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise the contribution of playwriting in the preservation of culture. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise the contribution of playwriting in the preservation of culture.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise the contribution of playwriting in the preservation of culture. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing - Plays is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing - Plays”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: explain the features of a play for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing - Plays to a partner. (skill: write a short play based on the theme for communication)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: recognise the contribution of playwriting in the preservation of culture)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing - Plays to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain the features of a play for information.
3. Practise this skill: write a short play based on the theme for communication.
4. Practise this skill: recognise the contribution of playwriting in the preservation of culture.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing - Plays from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing - Plays: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing - Plays?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does a play differ from a story?
2. How are plays written?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing - Plays means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain the features of a play for information.
5. Be able to: write a short play based on the theme for communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
